ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the image: In the image, Canada's major railways are represented by thick black lines, overall showing an east-west belt-like distribution, mainly concentrated in southern Canada, in the area near the U.S. border; the railways are densest near the Great Lakes-St. Lawrence River in the southeast. The cities marked on the map, such as Vancouver, Winnipeg, Toronto, Ottawa, Montreal, Halifax, etc., are also mostly distributed along the southern railway belt. Then reason: The common distribution pattern of railways and cities is more in the south and fewer in the north, especially concentrated along the southern border and in the southeastern region. Among Canada's human geographic elements, population is also mainly concentrated along the southern border and along the Great Lakes-St. Lawrence River line, so what is similar to the distribution pattern of railways and cities is population distribution.
